bytes.kicker: Textiles · 20 yarn, fabric and home-textile makers, 7 apparel makers
bytes.title: Textile makers widened margins. Apparel barely grew.
bytes.dek: Yarn, fabric and home-textile makers grew revenue a median 27% with margins up 1.6 points; apparel makers grew 5.5%.
bytes.read: In textiles the upstream makers are turning growth into margin, while apparel makers have barely grown.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: 'Textile makers' = companies classified as Other Textile Products (yarn, fabric, home and technical textiles); apparel = Garments & Apparels. Only companies whose calls Vantage reads; the chart shows up to 12 largest by market cap. Small groups: read medians as indicative.

stats.note: 13 of 18 grew profit on 27% revenue growth.

stats.label: Apparel makers' revenue
stats.note: Margin +0.2 pt across 7 companies.

stats.label: Textiles' net guidance

bytes.kicker: What managements talk about · Q4 FY26 → Q2 FY27 calls
bytes.title: Tariff talk is fading. Defence and data centres are rising.
bytes.dek: With US tariffs on India cut to 18% under the February 2026 trade deal and talks still running, tariffs came up on 22.5% of Q2 calls, down from 32.3% two quarters ago.
bytes.read: Managements have stopped explaining tariffs and started talking about where new orders come from: defence, data centres and customers moving supply chains to India.
bytes.sources: Vantage theme tracker across ~1,100 calls a quarter (BSE filings), as of 18 Nov 2026; tariff level: White House fact sheet on the US–India trade deal, Feb 2026
bytes.notes: Each call is tagged with the themes management discusses; a theme's share is the % of that quarter's calls that mention it. Shown: the six biggest risers and six biggest fallers between Q4 FY26 (calls in Apr–Jun 2026) and Q2 FY27 (Oct–Nov 2026). A mention is not a forecast: tariffs falling off calls means less discussion, not that tariff risk is gone. Open Themes on the dashboard for the companies behind each theme.

stats.label: Calls discussing tariffs
stats.note: 369 calls in Q4 FY26, 306 in Q1 FY27, 254 in Q2 FY27.

stats.label: Defence indigenisation
stats.note: Mentioned on 93 Q2 FY27 calls, up from 80; mostly industrial and defence suppliers.

stats.label: Data-centre power & cooling
stats.note: 110 Q2 FY27 calls, led by electrical equipment and industrial products makers.

bytes.kicker: Sterlite Technologies · Q2 FY27 results and call
bytes.title: Sterlite Tech's margin is nearing its FY29 target, two years early.
bytes.dek: Revenue rose 145% to ₹2,529 Cr and operational EBITDA margin reached 27.1%, so management lifted its FY29 target to about 30%, from 27%.
bytes.read: Orders, margins and guidance have all stepped up three calls in a row; the stock's fall after results says the market now wants proof the margins hold.
bytes.sources: Sterlite Technologies Q2 FY27 results (BSE, 23 Oct 2026) and Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; prices to 17 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: Margins are the company's operational EBITDA margins as stated on its calls; Q1 FY27 is derived from reported EBITDA (₹397 Cr) and revenue (₹1,910 Cr), and Q2 FY27 excludes the ₹161 Cr one-off tariff refund. Profit growth is flattered by that refund and a low base. The Q2 call flagged rising receivables and did not disclose utilisation. Not a recommendation.

stats.label: Open order book
stats.note: 4.6× the ₹7,687 Cr at the start of FY27; ₹18,618 Cr at end-Q1.

stats.label: Revenue growth
stats.note: ₹2,529 Cr in Q2 FY27. Reported EBITDA of ₹846 Cr includes a ₹161 Cr one-off US tariff refund.

stats.label: Share price since results
stats.note: From 23 Oct to 17 Nov, while the index rose 11%.

bytes.title: Specialty chemicals are back. Agrochemicals aren't.
bytes.dek: Specialty makers grew revenue a median 26% and widened margins; agrochemical companies' sales fell 1.3% and margins shrank.
bytes.read: The recovery is in specialty chemicals, not across the sector: agrochemical sales are still shrinking, and managements across chemicals are guarding H2 guidance.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026; sub-industries from company classification
bytes.notes: Specialty chemicals and pesticides & agrochemicals as classified for the companies whose calls Vantage reads. The chart shows the 12 largest specialty companies by market cap. Net guidance = % of chemical calls raising minus % cutting (Q2 FY27).

stats.label: Specialty: grew profit
stats.note: 31 of 37; median margin +0.7 pt.

stats.label: Agrochemicals: median revenue
stats.note: Margin -1.6 pt; 4 of 10 grew profit.

stats.label: Chemicals' net guidance
stats.note: Even so, more chemical managements cut guidance than raised it on Q2 calls (see the guidance byte).

bytes.kicker: Q2 FY27 results scorecard · 2,215 companies with margin data
bytes.title: Sales grew in every sector. Margins went nowhere.
bytes.dek: With the results deadline past, the median company grew revenue 16.9% year on year, but its operating margin moved just +0.1 points.
bytes.read: Growth came through at the top line but not into margins: costs and pricing absorbed most of it, so earnings grew roughly in line with sales.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: Revenue growth and operating (EBITDA) margin are year on year, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26, using each company's filed results. Medians, so a few large companies do not move the number. Banks and financial services are left out because their 'operating margin' is not comparable; sectors shown are the 14 with the most results filed. Open Results on the dashboard for every company.

stats.label: Half widened margins, half didn't
stats.note: 1,118 of 2,215 widened operating margin year on year; the rest held or shrank.

stats.label: Autos & components
stats.note: The fastest sales growth of any sector, yet the median margin slipped. 144 companies reported.

stats.label: Capital goods
stats.note: The largest group (499 companies): strong order-led growth with flat margins.

bytes.title: Only a third of stocks beat the market on results day.
bytes.dek: Even companies that grew profit 75% or more beat the index on the day after results only 46% of the time. The market wanted more than growth.
bytes.read: This season the bar was set before the numbers came out: misses were sold hard, and big beats were mostly already in the price.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and NSE/BSE closing prices, as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: Day-one reaction = the stock's move from the close before results to the close on the first trading day after, minus the benchmark index's move over the same day. Profit growth is net profit, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26; companies with no profit comparison are left out of the groups but counted in the overall share. Banks are excluded. Past reactions say nothing about future returns.

stats.label: Beat the index, all results
stats.note: 943 of 2,776 stocks outperformed the index on day one; the median stock lagged by 1.3%.

stats.label: Profit up 75% or more
stats.note: Strong growth barely tilted the odds: median day-one move -0.3% vs the index (387 stocks).

stats.label: Profit down 25% or more
stats.note: Misses were punished: median day-one move -2.5% vs the index (489 stocks).

bytes.kicker: Q2 FY27 results by company size · 2,891 companies
bytes.title: The bigger the company, the better the quarter.
bytes.dek: Half of micro-caps grew profit this season, against 74% of companies above ₹1 lakh crore, and large caps were the only group where most stocks beat the index on results day.
bytes.read: This season rewarded scale: larger companies grew profit more reliably and were rewarded for it, while the long tail of micro-caps lagged on both.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026; day-one reaction vs the benchmark index
bytes.notes: Market cap at the time results were filed; banks excluded. Micro-caps are many and volatile, so their median hides a wide spread. Results-day reaction = stock move on the first trading day after results minus the index move.

stats.label: Revenue growth: micro vs large
stats.note: Median for 1,769 micro-caps and 53 large caps.

stats.label: Large caps that beat the index on results day
stats.note: Against 33% of micro-caps.

stats.label: Micro-caps that grew profit
stats.note: 476 of 945 with a profit comparison.

bytes.kicker: Guidance direction · 1,128 Q2 FY27 calls read
bytes.title: Lenders guide up. Chemicals and FMCG guide down.
bytes.dek: Across 1,128 calls, 44% of managements cut or guided lower and 34% raised or guided higher. The split runs by sector, not by market.
bytes.read: Guidance is splitting by sector: lenders and auto makers sound confident, while chemicals, FMCG and IT are lowering the bar for H2.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of 1,128 Q2 FY27 earnings calls (BSE filings), as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: How it is counted: a call counts as raising when management raised a number it had guided before, or gave guidance that reads as positive; it counts as cutting when it cut a guided number or gave guidance that reads as negative. A call can count on both sides. Net = % raising − % cutting, per sector, for sectors with at least 25 Q2 FY27 calls read. Open Sectors → Guidance leaders for the companies behind each bar.

stats.label: Cut vs raised, all sectors
stats.note: 492 of 1,128 calls cut or guided lower; 387 raised or guided higher.

stats.label: Financial Services, net
stats.note: 64 of 144 lenders and financiers raised or guided up; 36 cut.

stats.label: Chemicals, net
stats.note: 46 of 73 chemical companies cut or guided lower; only 15 raised.

bytes.kicker: Aerospace & defence · 26 companies reported Q2 FY27
bytes.title: Defence revenue grew 42%. Private suppliers led.
bytes.dek: Order books are turning into revenue: the median defence company grew sales 42% year on year, and defence indigenisation came up on 93 Q2 calls, up from 80 two quarters ago.
bytes.read: The defence order cycle is now visible in revenue, and the smaller private suppliers of electronics, drones and components are converting it fastest.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026; theme counts from Vantage call tracker

bytes.kicker: Data-centre power & cooling · 110 Q2 FY27 calls
bytes.title: Everyone is talking data centres. The numbers aren't showing it yet.
bytes.dek: In capital goods, companies that discussed data centres grew revenue 27.8%, about the same as peers that didn't (27.4%).
bytes.read: Data-centre demand is real for a few suppliers, but as a theme it is crowded: mentioning it on a call has not yet meant faster growth than peers.
bytes.sources: Vantage theme tracker and Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE, as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: A call counts when management discusses data-centre power, cooling, cables or electrical equipment demand. The comparison uses capital goods companies whose Q2 FY27 calls Vantage read, split by whether the call discussed the theme. Mentions say nothing about how big data centres are in each company's revenue.

bytes.kicker: Autos · 55 component makers, 5 tyre makers, 5 two-wheeler makers
bytes.title: Auto parts grew 32%. Margins went the other way.
bytes.dek: Component makers grew revenue a median 32%, but the median operating margin slipped 0.5 points.
bytes.read: Volumes are not the question in autos this season; margins are. Recovery in H2 depends on passing higher costs through to customers.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026
